newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends in sharp slide on Brazil fallout.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends in sharp slide on Brazil fallout.

text.p: The Mexican peso ended steeply lower across the board on Tuesday.
Dealers said a sharp downturn in Brazilian equity markets fueled concerns of contagion in Mexican financial markets and triggered a speculative run on the peso.
Traders said speculative players also took advantage of brokers who had gone short dollars and had to cover positions.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 6.6 centavos weaker, respectively, at 7.9150/7.9250 and 7.9120/7.9220 per dollar.
"There was no direct pressure by foreigners on Mexico, but the (equity) markets in Brazil are plummeting and that is hitting us," a dealer said.
In Brazil, the Sao Paulo stock market Bovespa index .BVSP had fallen 1,001 points to 11,697 in late trade.
"There is a lot of pressure to devalue in Brazil... Speculators are using Brazil as a pretext and they caught many local brokers short dollars," the dealer added.
Same-day peso contracts closed trade mid-morning 1.6 centavos weaker at 7.8750/7.8800 per dollar.
Traders said rates could gain sharply at the central bank's Cetes auction later today in order to prevent the peso breaking the 8.00/per dollar barrier.
Banco de Mexico was expected to announce auction results at 1830 local time/2330 GMT.
